test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which year did the National Social Assistance Plan come into effect?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Social Assistance Plan (NSAP) was launched in August 1995.
 
• It provides social assistance benefits to poor households in the form of pensions and family benefit schemes.
 
• The plan includes schemes like the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), and the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS).
 
• The objective of NSAP is to ensure a minimum national standard for social assistance in addition to the benefits that states are currently providing or might provide in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)**

 
 
• It is a non-contributory pension scheme for persons above 60 years of age who belong to a below poverty line (BPL) family.
 
• The pension amount varies from state to state, with a minimum of Rs. 200 per month for individuals aged 60-79 and Rs. 500 for individuals aged 80 and above.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS)**
 
 
• This scheme provides a pension to widows aged 40-59 years who belong to BPL families.
 
• Under this scheme, a monthly pension of Rs. 300 is provided, which can vary based on the state government’s contributions.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS)**
 
 
• It provides pension to individuals aged 18-59 years with severe or multiple disabilities who belong to BPL families.
 
• The scheme offers a monthly pension of Rs. 300, which can be supplemented by the state government.
 
 
 
• **National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS)**
 
 
• This scheme provides a lump sum family benefit of Rs. 20,000 to the bereaved household in case of the death of the primary breadwinner aged between 18-59 years belonging to a BPL family.
